solution:
Split the bracket: \(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1}x+1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}=\sin^{-1}x+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\).

So the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[\sin^{-1}x+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right]dx\), which is of the form \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[f(x)+f'(x)\right]dx\) with \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}x\) and \(f'(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\).

Using \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[f(x)+f'(x)\right]dx=e^{x}f(x)+c\):

\(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1}x+1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)dx=e^{x}\sin^{-1}x+c\)

Verified by differentiating the answer back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x}\sin^{-1}x\right)=e^{x}\sin^{-1}x+e^{x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}=e^{x}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1}x+1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)\), which is the original integrand.

stem: If \(y = \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \cdots\infty}}}\), then show that \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{2y - 1}\).
solution:
Everything under the outermost radical, after the \(\sin x\), repeats the whole expression, so the radical is self-similar:

\(y = \sqrt{\sin x + y}\)

Squaring both sides gives an implicit relation between \(x\) and \(y\):

\(y^{2} = \sin x + y\)

Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\), treating \(y\) as a function of \(x\):

\(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos x + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

\(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos x\)

\((2y - 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos x\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\cos x}{2y - 1}\)

which is the required result.

**Independent check.** Solving \(y^{2} - y - \sin x = 0\) for the non-negative branch,

\(y = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{1 + 4\sin x}}{2}\)

Differentiating this explicitly,

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{4\cos x}{2\sqrt{1 + 4\sin x}} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sqrt{1 + 4\sin x}}\)

and since \(2y - 1 = \sqrt{1 + 4\sin x}\), this is the same expression as the one derived implicitly. The two routes agree.

Write \(\sec^{3}x=\sec x\cdot\sec^{2}x\) and integrate by parts with \(u=\sec x\), \(dv=\sec^{2}x\,dx\), so \(du=\sec x\tan x\,dx\) and \(v=\tan x\). Let \(I=\displaystyle\int\sec^{3}x\,dx\).

\(I=\sec x\tan x-\displaystyle\int\tan x\cdot\sec x\tan x\,dx=\sec x\tan x-\displaystyle\int\sec x\tan^{2}x\,dx\)

Using \(\tan^{2}x=\sec^{2}x-1\):

\(I=\sec x\tan x-\displaystyle\int\sec x\left(\sec^{2}x-1\right)dx=\sec x\tan x-\displaystyle\int\sec^{3}x\,dx+\displaystyle\int\sec x\,dx\)

\(I=\sec x\tan x-I+\log|\sec x+\tan x|\)

\(2I=\sec x\tan x+\log|\sec x+\tan x|\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\sec^{3}x\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\sec x\tan x+\dfrac{1}{2}\log|\sec x+\tan x|+c\)

Verified by differentiating the answer back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\sec x\tan x\right]=\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sec x\tan^{2}x+\sec^{3}x\right)\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\log|\sec x+\tan x|\right]=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\sec x\tan x+\sec^{2}x}{\sec x+\tan x}=\dfrac{1}{2}\sec x\). Adding, \(\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sec x(\sec^{2}x-1)+\sec^{3}x+\sec x\right)=\sec^{3}x\), the original integrand.

**(D)** \(\dfrac{1}{4}\)

Put \(t=4x-1\), so \(dt=4\,dx\), i.e. \(dx=\dfrac{dt}{4}\).

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{4x-1}=\dfrac{1}{4}\int\dfrac{dt}{t}=\dfrac{1}{4}\log|t|+c=\dfrac{1}{4}\log|4x-1|+c\)

Comparing with the given form \(A\log|4x-1|+c\) gives \(A=\dfrac{1}{4}\), which is option (D).

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{4}\log|4x-1|\right]=\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{4}{4x-1}=\dfrac{1}{4x-1}\).

**(A)**

A power of cosine is brought down to a first power by the triple-angle identity

\(\cos 3x = 4\cos^{3}x - 3\cos x\)

which rearranges to

\(\cos^{3}x = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\cos 3x + 3\cos x\right)\)

Hence

\(\displaystyle\int\cos^{3}x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{4}\int\cos 3x\,dx + \dfrac{3}{4}\int\cos x\,dx\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x + c\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{12}\sin 3x + \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x + c\)

which is option (A).

**Verification by differentiating the answer back:**

\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{12}\sin 3x + \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x\right] = \dfrac{3}{12}\cos 3x + \dfrac{3}{4}\cos x = \dfrac{1}{4}\cos 3x + \dfrac{3}{4}\cos x\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left(4\cos^{3}x - 3\cos x\right) + \dfrac{3}{4}\cos x = \cos^{3}x - \dfrac{3}{4}\cos x + \dfrac{3}{4}\cos x = \cos^{3}x\)

The integrand is recovered exactly, so (A) is confirmed. The other three options differ only in the coefficient of \(\sin x\); differentiating any of them leaves a stray \(\cos x\) term that does not cancel.

**(C)** \(\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(3x)+c\)

Take the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) out: \(9x^{2}+1=9\left(x^{2}+\dfrac{1}{9}\right)\), so

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{9x^{2}+1}=\dfrac{1}{9}\int\dfrac{dx}{x^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}}\)

Using \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^{2}+a^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}+c\) with \(a=\dfrac{1}{3}\):

\(=\dfrac{1}{9}\cdot 3\tan^{-1}(3x)+c=\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(3x)+c\), which is option (C).

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(3x)\right]=\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{3}{1+9x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{9x^{2}+1}\).

Put \(t=e^{x}\), so \(dt=e^{x}dx\) and \(e^{2x}=t^{2}\). Let \(I\) be the integral.

\(I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{5\,dt}{(t+1)\left(t^{2}+9\right)}\)

Resolve into partial fractions: \(\dfrac{5}{(t+1)(t^{2}+9)}=\dfrac{A}{t+1}+\dfrac{Bt+C}{t^{2}+9}\), so \(5=A\left(t^{2}+9\right)+(Bt+C)(t+1)\).

Put \(t=-1\): \(5=10A\), so \(A=\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Compare coefficients of \(t^{2}\): \(0=A+B\), so \(B=-\dfrac{1}{2}\).
Compare constants: \(5=9A+C\), so \(C=5-\dfrac{9}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\).

\(\therefore\ I=\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{t+1}-\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{t-1}{t^{2}+9}\,dt\)

Now \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{t-1}{t^{2}+9}\,dt=\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2t}{t^{2}+9}\,dt-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dt}{t^{2}+3^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left(t^{2}+9\right)-\dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{t}{3}\).

\(\therefore\ I=\dfrac{1}{2}\log|t+1|-\dfrac{1}{4}\log\left(t^{2}+9\right)+\dfrac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{t}{3}\)

Restoring \(t=e^{x}\):

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{5e^{x}}{\left(e^{x}+1\right)\left(e^{2x}+9\right)}dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left(e^{x}+1\right)-\dfrac{1}{4}\log\left(e^{2x}+9\right)+\dfrac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{e^{x}}{3}+c\)

Verified by differentiating the answer back. With \(t=e^{x}\) the derivative is
\(\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{t}{t+1}-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{t^{2}}{t^{2}+9}+\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{t}{t^{2}+9}=\dfrac{t}{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{t+1}-\dfrac{t-1}{t^{2}+9}\right]=\dfrac{t}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\left(t^{2}+9\right)-\left(t^{2}-1\right)}{(t+1)\left(t^{2}+9\right)}=\dfrac{5t}{(t+1)\left(t^{2}+9\right)}\),
which is the original integrand.

stem: The value of \(\int x^{x}(1 + logx)dx\) is equal to __________.
solution:
**(D)** \(x^{x}+c\)

Let \(y=x^{x}\). Taking logarithms, \(\log y=x\log x\).

Differentiating both sides with respect to \(x\): \(\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}+\log x=1+\log x\).

\(\therefore\ \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{x}\right)=x^{x}\left(1+\log x\right)\)

So the integrand is exactly the derivative of \(x^{x}\), and

\(\displaystyle\int x^{x}\left(1+\log x\right)dx=x^{x}+c\), which is option (D).

The differentiation above IS the check: the answer differentiated back reproduces the integrand.

Let \(t=x^{10}\), so \(dt=10x^{9}dx\), i.e. \(x^{9}dx=\dfrac{dt}{10}\).

\(\displaystyle\int x^{9}\sec^{2}\left(x^{10}\right)dx=\dfrac{1}{10}\displaystyle\int\sec^{2}t\,dt=\dfrac{1}{10}\tan t+c\)

Restoring \(t=x^{10}\):

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int x^{9}\sec^{2}\left(x^{10}\right)dx=\dfrac{1}{10}\tan\left(x^{10}\right)+c\)

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{10}\tan\left(x^{10}\right)\right]=\dfrac{1}{10}\sec^{2}\left(x^{10}\right)\cdot 10x^{9}=x^{9}\sec^{2}\left(x^{10}\right)\).

Take the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) out: \(25-9x^{2}=9\left(\dfrac{25}{9}-x^{2}\right)\), so

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{25-9x^{2}}dx=\dfrac{1}{9}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{2}-x^{2}}\)

Using \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{a+x}{a-x}\right|+c\) with \(a=\dfrac{5}{3}\):

\(=\dfrac{1}{9}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\cdot\frac{5}{3}}\log\left|\dfrac{\frac{5}{3}+x}{\frac{5}{3}-x}\right|+c=\dfrac{1}{30}\log\left|\dfrac{5+3x}{5-3x}\right|+c\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{25-9x^{2}}dx=\dfrac{1}{30}\log\left|\dfrac{5+3x}{5-3x}\right|+c\)

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{30}\left(\log|5+3x|-\log|5-3x|\right)\right]=\dfrac{1}{30}\left[\dfrac{3}{5+3x}+\dfrac{3}{5-3x}\right]=\dfrac{1}{10}\cdot\dfrac{(5-3x)+(5+3x)}{25-9x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{25-9x^{2}}\).

stem: If \(u\) and \(v\) are two functions of \(x\), then prove that \(\int uvdx = u\int vdx - \int\left\lbrack \frac{du}{dx}\int vdx \right\rbrack dx\).
solution:
Let \(u\) and \(v\) be functions of \(x\), and write \(w=\displaystyle\int v\,dx\), so that \(\dfrac{dw}{dx}=v\).

By the product rule of differentiation,

\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\,w\right)=u\dfrac{dw}{dx}+w\dfrac{du}{dx}=uv+\dfrac{du}{dx}\displaystyle\int v\,dx\)

Integrating both sides with respect to \(x\), and using \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(u\,w\right)dx=u\,w\):

\(u\displaystyle\int v\,dx=\displaystyle\int uv\,dx+\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{du}{dx}\displaystyle\int v\,dx\right]dx\)

Transposing,

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int uv\,dx=u\displaystyle\int v\,dx-\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{du}{dx}\displaystyle\int v\,dx\right]dx\)

which is the required result. (Here \(u\) is the first function and \(v\) the second; the arbitrary constant of the inner integration cancels between the two terms, so \(w\) may be taken with constant zero.)

stem: If \(u\) and \(v\) are differentiable functions of \(x\), then prove that \(\int udv = uv - \int vdu\). Hence evaluate \(\int logxdx\).
solution:
**Proof.** Let \(u\) and \(v\) be differentiable functions of \(x\). By the product rule,

\(d(uv)=u\,dv+v\,du\)

Integrating both sides,

\(\displaystyle\int d(uv)=\displaystyle\int u\,dv+\displaystyle\int v\,du\), i.e. \(uv=\displaystyle\int u\,dv+\displaystyle\int v\,du\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int u\,dv=uv-\displaystyle\int v\,du\)

**Hence \(\displaystyle\int\log x\,dx\).** Write \(\displaystyle\int\log x\,dx=\displaystyle\int\log x\cdot 1\,dx\) and take

\(u=\log x\), \(dv=dx\), so \(du=\dfrac{1}{x}dx\) and \(v=x\).

\(\displaystyle\int\log x\,dx=x\log x-\displaystyle\int x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}dx=x\log x-\displaystyle\int 1\,dx\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\log x\,dx=x\log x-x+c\)

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\log x-x\right)=\log x+x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}-1=\log x\).

Take \(\tan^{-1}x\) as the first function and \(x\) as the second (by LIATE, the inverse-trigonometric factor comes first). Let \(I=\displaystyle\int x\tan^{-1}x\,dx\).

\(I=\tan^{-1}x\displaystyle\int x\,dx-\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{-1}x\right)\displaystyle\int x\,dx\right]dx\)

\(=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{1+x^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\,dx\)

\(=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1+x^{2}-1}{1+x^{2}}\,dx\)

\(=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\left[1-\dfrac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right]dx\)

\(=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\dfrac{1}{2}\left[x-\tan^{-1}x\right]+c\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int x\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x+c\)

Verified by differentiating back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\tan^{-1}x-\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x\right]=x\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac{x^{2}}{2\left(1+x^{2}\right)}-\dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2\left(1+x^{2}\right)}=x\tan^{-1}x+\dfrac{x^{2}+1}{2\left(1+x^{2}\right)}-\dfrac{1}{2}=x\tan^{-1}x\).

Write \(\displaystyle\int\log x\,dx=\displaystyle\int\log x\cdot 1\,dx\) and integrate by parts with \(\log x\) as the first function and \(1\) as the second.

\(\displaystyle\int\log x\cdot 1\,dx=\log x\displaystyle\int 1\,dx-\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log x\right)\displaystyle\int 1\,dx\right]dx\)

\(=x\log x-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{1}{x}\cdot x\,dx=x\log x-\displaystyle\int 1\,dx\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\log x\,dx=x\log x-x+c\)

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\log x-x\right)=\log x+x\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}-1=\log x\), the original integrand.

Split the bracket: \(\dfrac{x+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}+1\).

Put \(t=\sin^{-1}x\), so \(x=\sin t\), \(\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\cos t\) and \(dx=\cos t\,dt\).

\(\displaystyle\int e^{\sin^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}+1\right)dx=\displaystyle\int e^{t}\left(\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t}+1\right)\cos t\,dt=\displaystyle\int e^{t}\left(\sin t+\cos t\right)dt\)

This is of the form \(\displaystyle\int e^{t}\left[f(t)+f'(t)\right]dt=e^{t}f(t)+c\) with \(f(t)=\sin t\), \(f'(t)=\cos t\):

\(=e^{t}\sin t+c\)

Restoring \(t=\sin^{-1}x\), so that \(\sin t=x\):

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int e^{\sin^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{x+\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)dx=x\,e^{\sin^{-1}x}+c\)

Verified by differentiating back: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\,e^{\sin^{-1}x}\right)=e^{\sin^{-1}x}+x\,e^{\sin^{-1}x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}=e^{\sin^{-1}x}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}+x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\right)\), the original integrand.

stem: Prove that: \(\int\sqrt{x^{2} - a^{2}}dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^{2} - a^{2}} - \frac{a^{2}}{2}\log\left| x + \sqrt{x^{2} - a^{2}} \right| + c\).
solution:
Let \(I=\displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\,dx=\displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\cdot 1\,dx\) and integrate by parts, taking \(\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\) as the first function and \(1\) as the second.

\(I=\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\displaystyle\int 1\,dx-\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\displaystyle\int 1\,dx\right]dx\)

\(=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2x}{2\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\cdot x\,dx=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\,dx\)

Write \(x^{2}=\left(x^{2}-a^{2}\right)+a^{2}\):

\(I=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\left(x^{2}-a^{2}\right)+a^{2}}{\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\,dx=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-\displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\,dx-a^{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\)

Using the standard result \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}=\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right|\):

\(I=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-I-a^{2}\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right|\)

\(2I=x\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-a^{2}\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right|\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\,dx=\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}-\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right|+c\)

Verified by differentiating the right-hand side back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}+\dfrac{x^{2}}{2\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}=\dfrac{2x^{2}-a^{2}}{2\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\), and
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[-\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\right|\right]=-\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}=-\dfrac{a^{2}}{2\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}\).
Adding, \(\dfrac{2x^{2}-2a^{2}}{2\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}}=\sqrt{x^{2}-a^{2}}\), as required.

Let \(I=\displaystyle\int\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\,dx=\displaystyle\int\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\cdot 1\,dx\) and integrate by parts, taking \(\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\) as the first function and \(1\) as the second.

\(I=\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\displaystyle\int 1\,dx-\displaystyle\int\left[\dfrac{d}{dx}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\displaystyle\int 1\,dx\right]dx\)

\(=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}-\displaystyle\int\dfrac{-2x}{2\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\cdot x\,dx=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x^{2}}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\,dx\)

Write \(x^{2}=a^{2}-\left(a^{2}-x^{2}\right)\):

\(I=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+\displaystyle\int\dfrac{a^{2}-\left(a^{2}-x^{2}\right)}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\,dx=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+a^{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}-\displaystyle\int\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\,dx\)

Using \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}=\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\):

\(I=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+a^{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}-I\)

\(2I=x\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+a^{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\,dx=\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}+\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)+c\)

Verified by differentiating the right-hand side back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}-\dfrac{x^{2}}{2\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}=\dfrac{a^{2}-2x^{2}}{2\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\), and
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\sin^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\right]=\dfrac{a^{2}}{2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}\).
Adding, \(\dfrac{2a^{2}-2x^{2}}{2\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}}=\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\), as required.

Split the bracket into two standard pieces:

\(\dfrac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sin^{2}x}=\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^{2}x}-\dfrac{\sin x}{\sin^{2}x}=\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x-\operatorname{cosec}x\)

So the integral is \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[\left(-\operatorname{cosec}x\right)+\left(\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x\right)\right]dx\), which is of the form \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[f(x)+f'(x)\right]dx\) with

\(f(x)=-\operatorname{cosec}x\) and \(f'(x)=\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x\)   (since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\operatorname{cosec}x=-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x\)).

Using \(\displaystyle\int e^{x}\left[f(x)+f'(x)\right]dx=e^{x}f(x)+c\):

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int e^{x}\left(\dfrac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)dx=-e^{x}\operatorname{cosec}x+c\)

Verified by differentiating back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(-e^{x}\operatorname{cosec}x\right)=-e^{x}\operatorname{cosec}x-e^{x}\left(-\operatorname{cosec}x\cot x\right)=e^{x}\operatorname{cosec}x\left(\cot x-1\right)=e^{x}\cdot\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\left(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}-1\right)=e^{x}\left(\dfrac{\cos x-\sin x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)\), the original integrand.

stem: Prove that: \(\int\frac{dx}{a^{2} - x^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\log\left| \frac{a + x}{a - x} \right| + c\).
solution:
Factorise the denominator and resolve into partial fractions:

\(\dfrac{1}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{(a-x)(a+x)}\)

Since \((a+x)+(a-x)=2a\),

\(\dfrac{1}{(a-x)(a+x)}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\cdot\dfrac{(a+x)+(a-x)}{(a-x)(a+x)}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\dfrac{1}{a-x}+\dfrac{1}{a+x}\right]\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a-x}+\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a+x}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[-\log|a-x|+\log|a+x|\right]+c\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{a+x}{a-x}\right|+c\)

Verified by differentiating the right-hand side back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2a}\left(\log|a+x|-\log|a-x|\right)\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\dfrac{1}{a+x}+\dfrac{1}{a-x}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\cdot\dfrac{(a-x)+(a+x)}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{a^{2}-x^{2}}\), as required.

subtopic: Integrals of the Type (px+q) over a Quadratic
solution:
Express the numerator in terms of the derivative of the denominator. Here \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{2}+4x+8\right)=2x+4\), so write

\(x=A(2x+4)+B\)

Comparing coefficients of \(x\): \(2A=1\), so \(A=\dfrac{1}{2}\). Comparing constants: \(4A+B=0\), so \(B=-2\).

Let \(I\) be the integral. Then

\(I=\dfrac{1}{2}\displaystyle\int\dfrac{2x+4}{x^{2}+4x+8}\,dx-2\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^{2}+4x+8}\)

The first integral is of the form \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}dx=\log|f(x)|\), so it equals \(\log\left|x^{2}+4x+8\right|\).

For the second, complete the square: \(x^{2}+4x+8=(x+2)^{2}+2^{2}\), and \(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{(x+2)^{2}+2^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+2}{2}\right)\).

\(\therefore\ I=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left|x^{2}+4x+8\right|-2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+2}{2}\right)+c\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{x}{x^{2}+4x+8}\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left(x^{2}+4x+8\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x+2}{2}\right)+c\)

(The modulus sign may be dropped because \(x^{2}+4x+8=(x+2)^{2}+4>0\) for all \(x\).)

Verified by differentiating back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\log\left(x^{2}+4x+8\right)\right]=\dfrac{x+2}{x^{2}+4x+8}\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x+2}{2}\right]=\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}}{1+\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{4}}=\dfrac{2}{x^{2}+4x+8}\).
Subtracting, \(\dfrac{(x+2)-2}{x^{2}+4x+8}=\dfrac{x}{x^{2}+4x+8}\), the original integrand.

stem: Prove that: \(\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2} + a^{2}}} = log\left| x + \sqrt{x^{2} + a^{2}} \right| + c\).
solution:
Put \(x=a\tan\theta\), so \(dx=a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta\) and

\(\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}=\sqrt{a^{2}\tan^{2}\theta+a^{2}}=a\sqrt{\sec^{2}\theta}=a\sec\theta\)   (taking \(a>0\) and \(\sec\theta>0\)).

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{a\sec^{2}\theta\,d\theta}{a\sec\theta}=\displaystyle\int\sec\theta\,d\theta=\log\left|\sec\theta+\tan\theta\right|+c_{1}\)

Now \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{x}{a}\) and \(\sec\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}{a}\), so

\(=\log\left|\dfrac{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}+x}{a}\right|+c_{1}=\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}\right|-\log a+c_{1}\)

Absorbing the constant \(-\log a\) into the constant of integration \(\left(c=c_{1}-\log a\right)\):

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}=\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}\right|+c\)

Verified by differentiating the right-hand side back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}\right|=\dfrac{1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}=\dfrac{\frac{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}+x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}}{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{2}+a^{2}}}\), as required.

stem: Prove that: \(\int\frac{dx}{a^{2} - x^{2}} = \frac{1}{2a}\log\left| \frac{a + x}{a - x} \right| + c\).
solution:
Factorise the denominator and resolve into partial fractions:

\(\dfrac{1}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{(a-x)(a+x)}\)

Since \((a+x)+(a-x)=2a\),

\(\dfrac{1}{(a-x)(a+x)}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\cdot\dfrac{(a+x)+(a-x)}{(a-x)(a+x)}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\dfrac{1}{a-x}+\dfrac{1}{a+x}\right]\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a-x}+\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a+x}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[-\log|a-x|+\log|a+x|\right]+c\)

\(\therefore\ \displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{a+x}{a-x}\right|+c\)

Verified by differentiating the right-hand side back:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[\dfrac{1}{2a}\left(\log|a+x|-\log|a-x|\right)\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\left[\dfrac{1}{a+x}+\dfrac{1}{a-x}\right]=\dfrac{1}{2a}\cdot\dfrac{2a}{a^{2}-x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{a^{2}-x^{2}}\), as required.
